newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES BEAT AND EMBARRASS ATHLETICS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES BEAT AND EMBARRASS ATHLETICS.

text.p: Red-hot Scott Erickson pitched a three-hitter and Rafael Palmeiro capped a four-run first inning with a three-run homer, leading the Baltimore Orioles to an 8-0 blanking of the Oakland Athletics in a game marked by a bench-clearing incident on Tuesday.
Erickson (14-5) walked one and struck out eight in his second shutout of the season.
Palmeiro went 3-for-4 after entering the game in a 3-for-41 slide.
Baltimore, which won for the 12th time in 15 games, lengthened its lead to 5 1/2 games over the second-place New York Yankees in the American League East.

The A's took exception to Reboulet stealing second in the sixth with Baltimore leading, 7-0. When Reboulet came to bat in the eighth, Oakland reliever Dane Johnson threw his first pitch behind Reboulet's head. Reboulet and catcher Brent Mayne exchanged words and both benches emptied. No punches were thrown, but umpire Jim Joyce ejected Reboulet and Mayne.
"I don't think it was right," Mayne said, "a team running with a 7-0 lead at that part of the game, period. That's it."
"No, I didn't throw at him," Johnson said. "The ball got away from me. Sometimes those things happen. My control has been off lately."
Oakland manager Art Howe was asked if Reboulet's stolen base had anything to with the incident.
"It might have hit a nerve," he said. "To get beat is one thing, but being embarrassed is another. Their pitcher was throwing a three-hitter."
In Boston, Bobby Witt (11-8) scattered 10 hits and rookie Fernando Tatis had four hits and four RBI as the Rangers clobbered the Boston Red Sox, 12-2.
Rookie Nomar Garciaparra went 2-for-5, extending his hitting streak to 15 games for the Red Sox.

In Chicago, Albert Belle ended a long power drought with two home runs, including a two-run shot in a three-run seventh inning that carried the Chicago White Sox to their third straight win, 8-5 over the Anaheim Angels.

Belle had not homered since July 18th and was coming off a 7-for-37 road trip. But he hit a solo shot in the bottom of the second to stake Chicago to a 1-0 lead. Belle had three hits, three RBI and scored three runs, and rookie Mario Valdez added two doubles and three RBI for the White Sox.
In New York, Dean Palmer homered and drove in four runs, and four relievers combined for four scoreless innings as the Kansas City Royals rallied for a 6-4 victory over the New York Yankees.

Palmer led off the sixth with his 17th homer to tie the game, 3-3, and his two-run double in the seventh put the Royals ahead for good, 5-4. He is hitting .404 (19-for-47) with 13 RBI in his last 12 games.
David Cone (12-6) was reached for five runs and eight hits in 6 1/3 innings.

In Seattle, Mike Matheny blasted a three-run homer and rookie Steve Woodard allowed three runs and four hits in seven innings as the Milwaukee Brewers won for just the third time in their last 11 games, 5-3 over the Seattle Mariners.

Seattle's Ken Griffey Jr. blasted his 37th homer of the season, a 456-foot blast into the third deck in right field in the sixth inning. It was the 275th career homer for Griffey, tying him with Roger Maris and Brian Downing for 89th on the all-time list.
In Toronto, Roger Clemens tossed an eight-hitter for his major league-leading 18th win, leading the Toronto Blue Jays to a 9-1 romp over the Minnesota Twins.

Clemens (18-4) walked just one as his ERA, also tops in the majors, dropped to 1.66. He entered the game with 2,792 career strikeouts, needing 12 to move past Cy Young into 13th place on the all-time list.
He fanned 10 going into the ninth and struck out Scott Stahoviak to open the frame.
Clemens struck out Marty Cordova looking to move past Young and, after giving up a double to Ron Coomer, notched his 13th strikeout and 2,805th of his career by fanning Rich Becker to end the game.

"Cito (Gaston) said something to me after the eighth about Cy Young," said Clemens. "I knew he wasn't talking about most innings pitched, but I guess I should have realised he (Young) was next on the list. As far as history goes, he's the guy. I mean, they named the greatest award in pitching after him."

In Cleveland, Manny Ramirez smacked a two-run homer and hot-hitting David Justice went 3-for-3 with two RBI as the Cleveland Indians won for the second time in eight games, 7-4, over the Detroit Tigers in a game delayed more than two hours by rain.
Eric Plunk (4-3) pitched two perfect innings, striking out three, for the victory and Jose Mesa worked a scoreless ninth for his fifth save.
